description: VESPER LABS is a team of two entrepreneurs from different backgrounds. Marie studied International Relations and specializes in Space Diplomacy, and Daniel studied Industrial Engineering and is a Mars Challenge 2026 winner. Together they combine their skills and knowledge from their respective fields to achieve outstanding results. They love business and innovation.
summary:
Vesper Atlas is a decision-support prototype that turns NASA’s PSI combustion data into one clear map. We converted 1,607 tests from 11 investigations into common units; 999 record both oxygen and pressure, so they can be plotted on the Atlas.

Users can enter their own cabin’s atmosphere, see which tests are closest, and check the expected lunar atmosphere (30%+ oxygen, 10.2 psi or less), where 66 tests fall. The tool also shows where evidence is missing, including partial gravity, for which PSI has no tests. An AI assistant answers in plain language, cites the investigation behind each answer, and says “no data” instead of guessing. A Standards and Treaties tab links the evidence to the NASA standards and space-law instruments related to crew safety.

It addresses the challenge by turning scattered microgravity combustion data into clear fire safety insights. It matters because the Moon’s atmosphere is expected to be richer in oxygen, which makes materials more flammable, and safety decisions need evidence. It is built to grow with new experiments such as LUCI and FM2.
details:
What it does. Vesper Atlas is a web tool that turns NASA’s PSI combustion data into one clear, searchable map. We converted 1,607 tests from 11 investigations into common units. The 999 tests that record both oxygen and pressure are plotted on the Atlas, with the expected lunar cabin atmosphere (30% oxygen or more, 10.2 psi or less) highlighted. Users can enter their own cabin’s atmosphere and see which tests are closest, look up each of the 23 PSI investigations we reviewed, compare up to three of them, and ask an AI assistant questions in plain language. The assistant cites the investigation behind every answer and replies “no data” when the evidence does not exist, instead of guessing. A Standards and Treaties section connects the evidence to the NASA standards and space-law instruments related to crew safety.

Benefits and impact. Fire safety decisions for future Moon cabins depend on evidence that is spread across many studies and tables. Vesper Atlas puts it in one place, shows where evidence is strong and where it is missing (for example, PSI has no tests in lunar or Martian gravity), and links it to the rules behind it. It is a decision-support prototype, not a certified system.

Tools. A single-page web application built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Data comes from NASA’s PSI repository. The AI assistant is a large language model, and we also used SI tools to help write and test our code.

What makes it creative. Instead of another simulator, we built a library for the evidence itself, with an honest “no data” rule, a cabin check, and a legal and standards layer from the space diplomacy side of our team.

Factors we considered. Safety (never overstate what the data shows), transparency (every figure traces to its source), and growth (the structure can take new experiments, such as LUCI and FM2, without being rebuilt).
